articles.title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio⁠ to beef up its biotech business
articles.summary: OpenAI says it's adding Orchestra's team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results.

articles.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
articles.summary: The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.

articles.summary: Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse hits 10M US downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
articles.summary: New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.

articles.title: Ex-Nvidia-turned-VC Amulya Vishwanath: ‘Physical AI is in its LEGO era’
articles.summary: It’s the moment everyone is waiting for — the ChatGPT moment for robotics, Amulya Vishwanath explained to TechCrunch’s Equity.

articles.title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web
articles.summary: Meta says it paused a Muse feature that lets you share conversations with the AI assistant after researchers found the URLs publicly available on the web, as reported by Ars Technica. In a report published this week, researchers at the security firm Claroc say they found more than 6,800 Muse links through public DNS records. […]

articles.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.summary: A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge. Though Norforge doesn't name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. Concerns over AI-powered cybersecurity breaches have grown […]

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

articles.title: This new qubit could be 100 times less error-prone in superfluid quantum computer breakthrough
articles.summary: A proposed qubit made with superfluid helium could cut quantum computing error rates by around 100 times by shielding quantum information from common forms of electromagnetic noise. If experiments confirm the predictions, the technology could eventually work alongside today’s superconducting qubits or serve as a new kind of quantum memory.

articles.title: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal
articles.summary: Researchers have shown that exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons can perform the full range of operations needed for universal quantum computing. Using 54 qubits on Quantinuum’s H2 processor, they combined braiding and fusion to unlock capabilities that braiding alone could not provide.

articles.title: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
articles.summary: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.

articles.title: New AI shopping agents promise better bargains. But who pays the price?
articles.summary: Meta's recently launched AI agent Muse promises to be many things: it can fire off emails, book vacations and fill out cumbersome online forms.

articles.title: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
articles.summary: On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or […]

articles.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
articles.summary: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year. That's according to an announcement on Tuesday that says Spotify has also made changes to its recommendation system to highlight more music made by human artists. "Our editors hold the same standard and […]

articles.title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
articles.summary: Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap. When the app detects a person, or a group of people, have their eyes closed in a photo it will automatically present users with a […]

articles.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
articles.summary: The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade while renewable energy growth slows down, a new report shows. Electricity demand is also climbing faster than it has in more than a decade with more data centers, factories, and electric vehicles plugging into the grid. Despite those growing demands, the […]

articles.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
articles.summary: CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition - when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they'd get from government bonds. Last Tuesday Chamath "SPAC King" Palihapitiya noticed the distressed debt, and also asked whether the AI buildout was a private credit bubble. […]

articles.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
articles.summary: Today, I’m talking with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, who has a lot of thoughts about AI, tech, and privacy. If you’ve been listening to the show, you know that one of my running theories is that those issues are driving a big and maybe kind of unexpected political realignment — and with the midterms coming […]

articles.title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
articles.summary: Democrats could win back control of Congress this November, and if they do, they'll need to decide how to approach one of the country's newest and thorniest political issues: AI. Polls predict Democrats will flip at least one chamber of Congress in the midterm elections, which would put committee leadership back in their hands. That […]

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary: A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.

articles.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
articles.summary: UCLA researchers built an AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos simultaneously, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy. Its speed, low energy demands, and resistance to attacks could make it a powerful tool for screening the growing flood of AI-generated video.

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.summary: A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. The technology could eventually enable miniature robots to search earthquake rubble and navigate dangerous spaces that conventional drones cannot reach.

articles.title: The shape behind the Einstein problem just revealed strange new physics
articles.summary: A mathematical shape famous for covering a surface without ever repeating has revealed an unexpected ability to twist light into unusual chiral patterns. The discovery could lead to new ways of controlling light, polarization, and advanced optical devices.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
articles.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue. Researchers cannot say the medications caused these problems, but the patterns may reveal overlooked signals worth studying.

articles.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
articles.summary: Scientists have created an ultra-small nanolaser that could eventually allow microchips to transmit information with light instead of electricity, potentially making computers faster while cutting energy use roughly in half. Thousands of the lasers could fit on a single chip, opening possibilities for more efficient data centers, smartphones, and advanced medical sensors.

articles.title: US regulators certify Boeing 737 MAX 10 after delays
articles.summary: U.S. officials gave final approval Tuesday to the Boeing 737 MAX 10, certifying the latest long-delayed version of the popular single-aisle aircraft.

articles.title: Digital natives are buying electric cars as if they were smartphones
articles.summary: Until recently, buying a car meant obsessing over horsepower, transmission types and brand heritage. But step into the market today and the showroom floor looks entirely different.

articles.title: The driveway divide: Why parking for electric vehicles is such a big barrier
articles.summary: Most people who have an electric car have access to a driveway or private parking. In England, 90% of EV owners can park easily and charge theirs from home. But roughly 40% of U.K. households don't have off-street parking, so the questions are how they would charge an EV and whether easy access to home charging would influence their decision to acquire one.

articles.title: Secret trigger words could make AI-powered robots dangerous
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) like OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and Google Gemini are increasingly being used to help robots perform tasks, but what if LLMs could be exploited to turn helpful robots into harmful robots?

articles.title: Ammonia-fueled ship exhaust treatment could achieve roughly 99% removal of targeted pollutants
articles.summary: A research team led by Dr. Sun-Mi Hwang from the Clean Air Research Laboratory at the Korea Institute of Energy Research (KIER) has developed catalysts as an all-in-one solution to address exhaust emissions from ammonia-fueled ships. This technology can simultaneously and cost-effectively remove various greenhouse gases from ammonia combustion and is expected to contribute to achieving carbon neutrality in the maritime industry.

articles.title: Single transistor design combines memory and signal processing for brain-inspired computing
articles.summary: As artificial intelligence moves increasingly toward edge devices, researchers are exploring electronic components that can combine memory and information processing. Memristive and synaptic devices are of particular interest because their electrical conductance can retain information about previous inputs, providing a physical basis for brain-inspired computing.

articles.title: Brain-inspired randomness makes artificial vision more reliable
articles.summary: Humans are usually remarkably good at recognizing objects, even under poor conditions. Artificial vision systems, by contrast, reach their limits more quickly. Researchers at the Hertie Institute for Clinical Brain Research have now investigated what artificial vision systems can learn from the brain. They found that combining two brain-inspired features can make image recognition considerably more reliable. The research findings are published in the journal Patterns.

articles.title: Background static can carry wireless data without an actively generated radio signal
articles.summary: Stanford researchers recently revealed how a seemingly physics-defying wireless communication technology works. The new technology, called thermal noise communication, harnesses background static that normally is the bane of radio, cellular and other wireless signals. In their new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the team showed how a transmitter could deliver data to a receiver without any actively produced signal by manipulating tiny oscillations in voltage.

articles.title: New method predicts iron ore behavior for lower-carbon steelmaking
articles.summary: Reducing carbon dioxide emissions from steelmaking requires more efficient ways to turn iron ore into iron. While hydrogen-based technologies offer a promising path toward lower-carbon steel production, conventional blast furnaces will remain important during the transition. Understanding how iron ore behaves inside these furnaces could help improve their efficiency and stability.
